title: 第21章 黄金的黎明第22章 工业的基础
slug: 军事公主不会爱上魔法科学家
lines: 凛冬城司法部的密谋，并未传到公爵府。
此时的府邸书房，灯火通明。
格雷森双眼布满血丝，但他整个人却处在一种极度亢奋的状态。
在他面前，是一张巨大的北境地图，上面用不同颜色的墨水标注着密密麻麻的符号。
“殿下，这是我连夜草拟的税制改革方案初稿。”
格雷森的声音沙哑，却透着一股前所未有的力量。
他将一叠厚厚的羊皮纸呈给瑟薇娅。
“按照洛加里斯教授的理论框架，我将税收分为三类：农业税、商业税、资产税。”
“第一，大量减少人头税和基础农业税。让所有农民和农奴，都能拥有自己土地上百分之九十五的收成！”
此言一出，旁听的维克多参谋呼吸一窒。
这是要动摇北境千百年来的根基。
格雷森没有理会他的反应，继续道：“第二，商业税，设立十五级阶梯税率。从城内的小摊贩，到跨越数个行省的商会，利润越高，税率越高。年利润超过十万金狮币的巨型商会，税率将达到百分之五十！”
维克多倒吸一口凉气。
这是要将那些大商人往死里逼。
“第三，土地持有税。名下土地超过一定数量，每多一亩，税率便以几何级数递增，最高达百分之六十！”
格雷森说完，整个书房落针可闻。
他这套方案，几乎是把刀架在了所有富裕阶层的脖子上。
瑟薇娅一页一页地翻看，银灰色的眼眸中，光芒越来越亮。
她只说了一个字。
“格雷森，我给你的人，够不够？”
“足够了，殿下。”格雷森躬身，“都是您从王都带来的心腹，能力与忠诚毋庸置疑。我们已经组建了三十支税务监察小队，随时可以派往北境各大城市。”
“那就去办。”瑟薇娅将方案递还给他，“三天之内，我要让这份公告，贴满北境每一座城市的公告栏。”
格雷森领命，带着一股使命感昂然退下。
第二天，凛冬城的公告栏前，人山人海。
当宣读官念出农业税的具体实施方案的那一刻，人群先是死一般的寂静，然后爆发出山呼海啸般的欢呼。
无数衣衫褴褛的平民、农人跪倒在地，冲着公爵府的方向嚎啕大哭。
“公主殿下万岁！”
“温特霍尔德家族万岁！”
与之形成鲜明对比的，是那些混在人群中的贵族管家和富商们。
他们听着那一条条针对自己的税法，脸上的血色一点点褪去，变得和北境的冬雪一样惨白。
反抗？
马库斯家族的血还没干透，那些钢铁怪物的影子，还在他们噩梦里徘徊。
凛冬城书房内，维克多参谋脸上的激动尚未完全褪去，但眉头却已紧锁。
他看向瑟薇娅，沉声开口：“殿下，税制改革安抚了民心，却也得罪了北境所有的商人和贵族。他们现在不敢动，但暗地里……”
“无妨。”瑟薇娅打断了他，“一群喂饱了的肥羊，在看到屠刀后，总会老实一段时间。”
她的声音很平静，仿佛在说一件与自己无关的小事。
“格雷森。”瑟薇娅转向一旁的临时财政总管。
“属下在。”格雷森立刻躬身。
“北境军团被拖欠的军饷和阵亡士兵的抚恤金，总共有多少？”
格雷森早有准备，立刻报出一个精确的数字：“回殿下，自三年前起，军团累计拖欠薪饷二十一万三千金狮币。历年积压的抚恤金，共计八万九千金狮币。合计三十万零两千金狮币。”
维克多参谋的拳头瞬间攥紧。
content_en:
The conspiracy of the Ministry of Justice in Winter City did not reach the Duke's Palace.
At this time, the study room of the mansion was brightly lit.
Grayson's eyes were bloodshot, but he was in an extremely excited state.
In front of him was a huge map of the North, with dense symbols marked with different colors of ink.
"Your Highness, this is the first draft of the tax reform plan that I drafted overnight."
Grayson's voice was hoarse, but it contained an unprecedented strength.
He presented a thick stack of parchment to Serviya.
“According to Professor Logaris’ theoretical framework, I divide taxes into three categories: agricultural taxes, commercial taxes, and asset taxes.”
"First, drastically reduce the poll tax and basic agricultural tax. Let all farmers and serfs own 95% of the harvest on their own land!"
As soon as these words came out, the listening staff officer Victor took a breath.
This is to shake the foundation of the Northern Territory that has existed for thousands of years.
Grayson ignored his reaction and continued: "Second, commercial tax, set up a fifteen-level stepped tax rate. From small vendors in the city to chambers of commerce spanning several provinces, the higher the profit, the higher the tax rate. For giant chambers of commerce with annual profits of more than 100,000 gold lion coins, the tax rate will reach 50%!"
Victor gasped.
This is to drive those big businessmen to death.
"Third, land holding tax. For every additional acre of land over a certain amount, the tax rate will increase geometrically, up to 60%!"
After Grayson finished speaking, the whole study could hear needles dropping.
His plan almost puts a knife on the necks of all wealthy people.
Serviya flipped through page after page, the light in her silver-gray eyes getting brighter and brighter.
"Okay."
She said only one word.
"Grayson, are the people I gave you enough?"
"That's enough, Your Highness." Grayson bowed, "They are all the confidants you brought from the royal capital. There is no doubt about their ability and loyalty. We have set up thirty tax inspection teams and can be sent to major cities in the north at any time."
"Then go ahead and do it." Serviya handed the plan back to him, "Within three days, I will have this announcement plastered all over the bulletin boards in every city in the north."
"Yes!"
Grayson accepted the order and retreated proudly with a sense of mission.
The next day, there was a sea of ​​people in front of the bulletin board in Winter City.
When the announcer read out the specific implementation plan of the agricultural tax, the crowd was silent at first, and then burst into cheers like a mountain roar and a tsunami.
Countless civilians and farmers in ragged clothes knelt on the ground, wailing in the direction of the Duke's Palace.
"Long live your Royal Highness the Princess!"
"Long live the Winterhold family!"
In sharp contrast, there are the noble housekeepers and wealthy businessmen mixed in the crowd.
As they listened to the tax laws targeting them, the blood on their faces faded little by little, becoming as pale as the winter snow in the north.
Resist?
The blood of the Marcus family has not dried yet, and the shadows of those steel monsters are still lingering in their nightmares.
…
In the study room of Winter City, the excitement on Staff Officer Victor's face has not completely faded away, but his brows are already furrowed.
He looked at Serviya and said in a deep voice: "Your Highness, the tax reform has appeased the people, but it has also offended all the merchants and nobles in the north. They dare not move now, but secretly..."
"It doesn't matter." Serviya interrupted him, "A group of well-fed fat sheep will always be honest for a while after seeing the butcher's knife."
Her voice was calm, as if she was talking about a trivial matter that had nothing to do with her.
"Grayson." Serviya turned to the temporary financial manager aside.
"My subordinate is here." Grayson immediately bowed.
"How much is the total arrears of military pay and pensions for fallen soldiers of the Northern Army?"
Grayson was well prepared and immediately reported an accurate figure: "Back to Your Highness, since three years ago, the legion has been owed a total of 213,000 gold lion coins in salary arrears. The backlog of pensions over the years totals 89,000 gold lion coins. The total is 302,000 gold lion coins."
Staff Officer Victor's fists clenched instantly.
